fixes.explanation: Gilgal, baker! Hosea 9:15 says, "All their evil appears at Gilgal, for there I hated them." That's a heavy line, and I think it's meant to be. The LORD says it plainly, so we let it sit.

City gates are a fair guess, friend, but this verse goes somewhere closer to home. Hosea 9:8 says, "Hostility is in the house of his God!" I think that's the part that makes you stop and read it twice. It's not out at the gates. It's in the house of his God.

Shiloh is a fair guess, friend, but this verse names a different place. Hosea 9:15 says, "All their evil appears at Gilgal, for there I hated them." I think a name like Shiloh sticks in your head because it sounds so familiar. Here the LORD points to Gilgal.

A peace treaty is a smart guess, friend, because that's how a lot of kings get in trouble. But this verse points to something closer to the heart. Hosea 9:17 says, "My God will reject them because they have not obeyed Him." The reason isn't a paper they broke. It's that they did not obey Him.
